uzo.purpose: Marks one option as yes or no inside a form; it applies when the form is sent: terms accepted, newsletter, remember me.

instead.kialo: A setting that applies at once is a switch, because a checkbox promises nothing until the form is sent; Fundamento covers it with sxaltilo.
One of a few options is a radio group, because checkboxes let a person tick several and the form could not tell which one counts; Fundamento has no such Ero yet (elekto, PR ③ of Spec 010).

boundary.kialo: A checkbox holds yes or no, because the form sends it or does not; a mixed state belongs to a group of checkboxes.
Several checkboxes stand in a form under a heading the form owns, because the heading names the question and each box one answer; Fundamento has no group Ero yet, so a person decides.
A checkbox without a visible label says that something is ticked, not what, because the box shows the answer and only the label names it.

containers.name: form
containers.kialo: A checkbox without a form has no sender, because its answer is only sent with the form.

containers.name: dialog
containers.kialo: A dialog may ask for a yes or no before it ends, because the decision it ends in may need it (terms accepted).

with.kialo: Checkboxes stand among the fields of a form, one below the other, because a person reads a form top down and answers it in that order.
The form ends with the button that sends it, because ticking a box does nothing by itself; the button stands after the last checkbox.

never.kialo: A checkbox stands in no slot of a button, because a button is one target with one name and the checkbox could not be reached on its own.
